dialog.body: Utilities billing, this is Tony. How can I help you?

Hi Tony, yeah, it's Celeste Spencer. I'm at 244 Gibbs Avenue, over on the Ocean Drive side. I got my water and sewer bill and, I mean, I'm a little annoyed, you know, because it covers a quarter. A whole quarter. Right?
Okay, Ms. Spencer, let me pull up your account. Gibbs Avenue, 244, got it. Yep, I see the latest bill here. What's the question on it?

Well, why is it a quarter? I'm used to getting something more regular, you know. And the dates on it, I mean, I can't tell how you count them. It says one date to another date and that's not three months by my math. Are you following me?

I follow you. So the bill is quarterly, meaning each one covers about three months of use. The dates on there are the meter reading dates, not the first and last of the month. So the period runs from the last time the meter was read to this time it was read. Sometimes that's a few days over or under three months depending on when the reader got to your street.
Okay, but that's what bugs me. So if the reader comes late, I pay for extra days. Right?
You pay for the water that went through the meter, so the extra days are just the extra water used in those days. It's not a separate charge. Nothing's being tacked on for the days themselves.
Hm. I mean, it still feels like a long stretch to be billed for all at once. You know, when you're budgeting.
I hear you. It's the way the billing cycle is set up, so I can't change that on your account. But I can tell you what the dates are on yours, if that helps you line things up.
No, no, I got the gist. Can you just send me a copy? A duplicate, by email? I think I tossed the envelope and the bill's got coffee on it. Don't ask.
No problem. I can email you a copy. What email address do you want it sent to?
Oh, um, do you have one on file already? I think I gave it once.
Let me look. [pause] I don't see an email on the account, just your phone. So I'll need one. Go ahead and spell it for me.
Okay. It's celeste dot spencer, all one word spelled S-P-E-N-C-E-R, at a mail dot com. Wait, no, sorry, it's at a-mail, with an A. A-M-A-I-L dot com. You got that?
Let me read it back. Celeste dot Spencer, S-P-E-N-C-E-R, at A-M-A-I-L dot com. Right?
Right, right. That's it.
Great. I'll send that over this afternoon. It should hit your inbox within a little while. If you don't see it, check the spam folder.
Okay. And one more thing. I work days, you know, so I'm never able to get to City Hall during the day. Can I pay in person after four thirty, or like in the evening? Is there any way to do that?

The counter closes in the afternoon, so after four thirty in person isn't going to work. But there are a few ways around that. You can pay online anytime, day or night, through the city's website. There's also a drop box outside City Hall for checks that's available after hours. And you can mail a check in.
The drop box, okay. Is that, like, safe? I mean, I just put the check in with the stub?
Yep. Check made out to the city, put your account number on the memo line, and drop in the stub if you've got it. Since you'll have the emailed copy, you can print that and use it.

Okay, good. Right. I can do that on my way home. Sorry, I'm distracted, I've got paint all over my hands. I'm doing a bedroom in this color called oatmeal. Which is just beige, I mean, let's be honest.
Oatmeal. Sounds nice and calm. Hope it goes on easy.
Eh, second coat tonight. Anyway, so the copy's coming today, and I can use the drop box. Is there anything else I need to know about the due date?
The due date's printed right on the bill, near the top by the amount due. It'll be on the emailed copy too. As long as it's in the box by then, you're fine.
Okay. Alright. I just wish it wasn't a whole quarter at once, but I get it, I guess.
Understood. Anything else I can help with today, Ms. Spencer?
No, that's it. Thanks, Tony.
You're welcome. Enjoy the rest of your lunch hour, and good luck with the second coat.
Thanks. Bye now.
